{{Quote|A droid for every purpose.|Industrial Automaton tagline|<ref name="HNN">[[HoloNet News (original website)|''HoloNet News'' website]]</ref>}}
'''Industrial Automaton (IA)''' was one of the two primary [[Droid/Legends|droid]] manufacturers in [[The galaxy/Legends|the galaxy]], the other being [[Cybot Galactica/Legends|Cybot Galactica]]. IA was a company specializing in droids for all trades and walks of life. Its most popular products were the [[R-series/Legends|R-series]] [[Astromech droid/Legends|astromech droids]], in particular the versatile [[R2-series astromech droid/Legends|R2-series]].

==History==
{{Quote|Machines For The Future.|Alternate Industrial Automaton tagline|<ref name="Star Wars: The Roleplaying Game (first edition)">[[Star Wars: The Roleplaying Game (first edition)|''Star Wars: The Roleplaying Game'']]</ref>}}
[[File:IA_Logo.svg|thumb|left|150px|Another IA logo]]
Industrial Automaton was formed over 850 years before the rise of the [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Empire]] with the merger of [[Industrial Intelligence/Legends|Industrial Intelligence]] and [[Automata Galactica/Legends|Automata Galactica]]. While not competitors, these two corporations were not friendly with each other. Working relations between them strained amid the rampant rumors as to how Automata Galactica acquired the economic strength to purchase Industrial Intelligence. As a result, the higher executives at Industrial Intelligences sealed away their most top-secret projects in a highly encrypted memory vault. Automata Galactica spent years trying to decipher the encryption programs and eventually managed to slice into some of the files. One of the files they found detailed the [[Intellex ship-configuration computer|Intellex]] computer configuration. This compact computer system could adapt to improve existing computer configurations, and was originally designed as an advanced advisory "housekeeping" system for starships. As a dedicated droid hardware manufacturer, Automata Galactica took the computer system and [[Intellex|implanted it]] into a prototype maintenance droid called the [[P2-series astromech droid|P2]], the first of Industrial Automaton's [[Astromech droid/Legends|astromech droids]].<ref>{{JournalCite|7|The History of R-Series Astromech Droids}}</ref> Industrial Automaton became a vastly wealthy company, and vied for control of the droid market with fellow manufacturing giant Cybot Galactica. These rival companies were known as the "Big Two" of droid production. IA was known for its high-precision merchandise and deep discounts, and was ruthless enough to survive during the reign of the Galactic Empire. The company was also one of the first Contributing Sponsors of the [[Corporate Sector Authority/Legends|Corporate Sector Authority]]. IA maintained factories in many locations, including [[Rordis City]] on [[Nubia/Legends|Nubia]].<ref name="Hnn45" />

Industrial Automaton came to monopolize the droid market through production of its most popular creation; the R-series astromech droids. While early models were deemed a critical failure, IA's R2-series astro-droid became beloved across the galaxy. The success of the R2 led to further R-series models, including the [[R4 astromech droid/Legends|R4]] units often used as navigators by [[Jedi/Legends|Jedi]] [[Starfighter/Legends|starfighter]] pilots, and, during the era of the [[New Republic/Legends|New Republic]], the advanced [[R7-series astromech droid|R7]] and [[R8-series astromech droid|R8]] models. While these designs proved successful, others were not so well received; Industrial Automaton was forced to cancel production of its [[R5-series astromech droid|R5-series]] droids after poor sales,<ref name="Hnn45" /> and later limited the warranty on astromech booster rockets after a series of injuries caused by falling droids.<ref name="Hnn55">{{HoloNetNewsWeb|55|business/1359_2.html|IA Caps Droid Rocket Warranty at 20 Years}}</ref>

[[File:IndustrialAutomatonAd-HNNVol531-45.gif|thumb|right|250px|An IA advertisement that appeared in [[HoloNet News/Legends|HoloNet News]].]]
Despite these minor setbacks, Industrial Automaton remained a constant presence in the droid market, thanks not only to its astromech designs, but also to the rest of its varied production line. Industrial Automaton created [[Protocol droid/Legends|protocol droids]] such as the [[LOM-series protocol droid/Legends|LOM-series]] and the [[SE4 servant droid]], labor droids including [[ASP-series labor droid/Legends|ASPs]] and [[FLR-series Logger Droid|FLR Loggers]], and security droids in the form of [[Mark IV sentry droid/Legends|Mark IVs]] and [[Hound-W2 SPD]] units. In addition to its droids designs, IA produced a number of automated devices, including targeting computers, that were powered by droid brains.

Prior to the [[Dark Nest Crisis]], Industrial Automaton produced the [[R9-series astromech droid|R9-series astromech]], though during the conflict, the company was purchased by [[Bornaryn Trading]], owned by [[Aryn Dro Thul]].
